applies_why: The judge text decides a single-verse point as UNDERDETERMINED because Matthew 1:16 admits two readings, which is what K-S2 governs.
quote: UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: The phrase 'A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand' — I weighed whether 'admits both ... readings' means a single verse leaving the question open (a forbidden ground) or a two-sense verse whose senses both stand, not an UNDERDETERMINED finding.
why: Because the judge labels the point UNDERDETERMINED on the ground that Matthew 1:16 admits both readings, it treats a two-sense verse as open rather than letting both senses stand as K-S2 requires.
